{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In the area of [[mathematics]] known as [[semigroup theory]], an '''''E''-semigroup''' is a [[semigroup]] in which the [[idempotent]]s form a [[subsemigroup]].<ref name="W">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1007/s002330010131| title = Certain congruences on E-inversive E-semigroups| journal = [[Semigroup Forum]]| volume = 65| issue = 2| pages = 233–248| year = 2002| last1 = Weipoltshammer | first1 = B. }}</ref>

Certain classes of ''E''-semigroups have been studied long before the more general class, in particular, a [[regular semigroup]] that is also an ''E''-semigroup is known as an [[orthodox semigroup]].

Weipoltshammer proved that the notion of [[weak inverse]] (the existence of which is one way to define [[E-inversive semigroup|''E''-inversive semigroup]]s) can also be used to define/characterize ''E''-semigroups as follows: a semigroup ''S'' is an ''E''-semigroup if and only if, for all ''a'' and ''b'' ∈ ''S'', ''W''(''ab'') = ''W''(''b'')''W''(''a''), where ''W''(''a'') ≝ {''x'' ∈ ''S'' | ''xax'' = ''x''} is the set of weak inverses of ''a''.<ref name="W"/>
